changelog_text:
**Notable changes:**

- **Flight Recorder** - The Flight Recorder is a replay feature that records the direct game render without the game HUD layer or any imgui elements at all. The game HUD can be used during the recorded flight, and will still not be visible in the replay. By default, this feature includes the telemetry overlay. After recording is complete, the finalization step composites the telemetry overlay onto the video. Because all of the telemetry has already been recorded by this point, the overlay clock is synced to liftoff and all mission events are placed ahead of time where they happened. This step can be disabled in the mod settings. Recording can be started/stopped by keybind (F9 by default), or by a button in the mod settings. This features relies on ffmpeg being present on the user's machine and either listed in the PATH or manually pointed to from the settings.
- **Addon Support** - I don't expect to see this used by other modders (although they can!), but this functionality allows a seperate mod to act as a component of the main mod when installed, to add extra functionality. I have an upcoming experimental feature that uses this which is why it was added, TBD when or if that will be released.
- **Engine Diagram Scaling** - Changes have been made to how the engine dots in the diagram are scaled. Engine scale is still correct relative to other engines, but the scaling of the dots has been tweaked to make them fill up the avalible space whenever possible. This resolves an issue that sometimes occured with certain engine configurations where the scaling of the dots left a strange amount of unfilled space. Notably this would occur with a Starship engine bay re-creation with the three small engines and three large ones.
- **Landing Burn Detection Fix** - Once a landing burn is detected, the event system will not allow additional landing burn events to appear for that stage. This fixes an issue where the event timeline would be spammed with landing burns if the player turned the engines on and off multiple times.

listing.name: Webcast Telemetry Overlay
listing.abstract: A SpaceX-style launch broadcast telemetry overlay in-game
listing.description:
A work-in-progress mod for Kitten Space Agency that creates a SpaceX-style launch broadcast telemetry overlay in-game. The overlay is populated with live data from the active vehicle and the mod includes an engine diagram generated automatically using the actual position of the engines on your stage relative to each other.

![Screenshot 1](ksa-image:9e-hero-newnew)

## The mod features:

- A bottom telemetry bar: speed and altitude on the left, T+ clock and mission timeline in the center, g-force and the engine diagram on the right. All of these positions are configurable. Styled to look like the SpaceX webcast overlay, slick animations and all.
- An engine diagram built from the real nozzle positions on your active stage, with a propellant arc gauge around it. It intelligently displays the engines on the current stage, and filters out thngs like verniers and RCS nozzles. Engines are displayed to scale with each other based on exit diameter.
- Event notifications for certain in-flight events. Currently: Liftoff, Max-q, MECO, Stage Sep, SES-1, SECO, Landing burn, landing, and generic engine ignition/cutoff. I am not totally happy with how this works for now, it's not fully reliable but it does work most of the time. Improvements coming eventually, but it can be disabled in settings.
- A mission timeline bar showing detected events behind the marker and any planned maneuvers ahead of it.
- Freeze-on-signal-loss: if the vehicle stops being controllable, the overlay freezes at the last received values. When a vehicle passes 95% tolerance on any load limit, the telemetry pre-emptively freezes until either the vehicle breaks apart or the tolerance falls back below 95%. This prevents garbage telemetry being used from the same frame as a vehicle failure.
- Optionally and by default hides the flight UI while the overlay is up, and restores it afterwards. The HUD is shown again while the game's own layout-saving window is open, so a HUD layout saved with the overlay running does not have everything switched off.
- Every element is available as its own movable imgui window that behaves like any other.
- Fairly in-depth configuration available in the settings menu.

![Unusual engine layout example](ksa-image:funky)
![Extreme engine count example](ksa-image:72e)

## Installation

I recommend installing via Borea (that's where you are right now!). Alternatively you can download from Github or from Spacedock.
If installing manually:

Extract into `Documents/My Games/Kitten Space Agency/mods/` and add to `manifest.toml`:

```toml
[[mods]]
id = "KSATelemetryOverlay"
enabled = true
```

## Dependencies:
StarMap is required for this mod. Borea provides Starmap by default.

[ModMenu](https://ksamodding.github.io/Borea/mod/ModMenu/) is optional but recommended, it provides the settings dropdown menu. If modmap is not installed, the settings menu can be accessed through a keybind that brings up a dedicated window, by default **numpad backslash**

## Settings

Toggle the overlay on and off using the **numpad period** key by default. This can be configured in the config file or the settings menu.

Settings are saved to `Documents/My Games/Kitten Space Agency/KSATelemetryOverlay/config.json`, which is safe to edit by hand if your heart so desires.
